## Summary
- Stacked on #8891. This branch now includes that pull request through `894a2b72`. The new delta is ZeRO-3 and the dedicated ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer.
- `load_checkpoint` still always restores saved fp32 masters. `load_optimizer_states=False` keeps those masters and starts Adam with fresh moments. `load_module_only=True` rebuilds the dedicated BF16 optimizer from the loaded bf16 weights. ZeRO-3 still reads its fp32 partition on a module-only load, because the model checkpoint does not hold the partitioned weights.
- `ZeRO-3` and `BF16_Optimizer.load_state_dict(..., load_from_fp32_weights=False)` now rebuild the masters from the bit16 weights, matching ZeRO stage 1 and 2. `DeepSpeedEngine.load_checkpoint` passes true, so a normal resume keeps the saved masters. `zero_optimization.load_from_fp32_weights` stays deprecated and ignored.

AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. This does not duplicate an open DeepSpeed PR.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/unit/checkpoint/test_fp32_master_stage3_bf16.py` with torch 2.9.1+cu130, Python 3.12.12, gloo, world size 1, commit `b190a3f7`: 2 passed. The dedicated BF16 optimizer keeps the saved masters when optimizer state is skipped and rebuilds them for `load_module_only=True`. ZeRO-3 keeps the saved masters for both of those loads. Adam moments stay fresh.
- [ ] Not run on the 4×H200 node. The #8891 suite there does not cover these two optimizers.

Validated cells: dedicated ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer and ZeRO-3, same data-parallel size, legacy checkpoint, bf16, no offload. Open cells: fp16, MoE, NVMe offload, and a data-parallel size change.

Merging master would shrink the diff to those three files. It merges cleanly with master.

The branches look right to me, but the new test doesn't reach them. `DeepSpeedEngine.load_checkpoint` always passes `load_from_fp32_weights=True`, and the test only loads through the engine. I ran a copy of `test_fp32_master_stage3_bf16.py` on CPU (gloo) with a client `torch.optim.Adam`, since DeepSpeed's fused Adam can't build on my machine. It passes on this branch and also on master without it.

Calling the optimizer directly does show the change. After a module-only load, I nudged the masters and then called `engine.optimizer.load_state_dict(sd_list, load_optimizer_states=False, load_from_fp32_weights=False)`:
- On this branch, both the BF16 optimizer and ZeRO-3 end with the saved masters rounded to bf16, i.e. rebuilt from the bit16 weights.
- On master, the BF16 optimizer keeps the stale nudged masters, and ZeRO-3 keeps the unrounded saved masters.

A test along those lines would pin the new behaviour.

Minor: ZeRO-3's universal load honours `False` only with optimizer states. Without them, it calls `load_module_checkpoint_state_from_checkpoint_dir_stage3(checkpoint_folder, True)`. The BF16 and ZeRO-1/2 universal loads ignore the flag. That path isn't reachable from the engine today, so it may not matter.

The engine never passes `load_from_fp32_weights=False`, so this branch is only reachable through a direct `load_state_dict` call. The new test goes through `load_checkpoint` and passes on master too. A direct call after a module-only load would cover it: the masters should end up equal to the bf16 weights.
